acceptance_criteria: This preregistration is the sole file introduced by the first branch commit and is externally anchored before implementation.
Primary-source transcription and locators are independently checkable.
The experimental covariance feasibility verdict is derived from exact source-bound matrix checks.
The Bayesian consensus feasibility verdict is derived from an explicit inventory of specified versus missing result-driving choices.
No BIPM-vs-NIST numerical compatibility test is performed.
One complete Python suite, relevant guards, and git diff --check pass on the final tree.

decision_policy.common_constant_comparison: Out of scope for this feasibility PR. Any BIPM-14 vs NIST-26 common-constant test requires a later preregistration with an explicit cross-measurement model and evidence boundary.
decision_policy.experimental_covariance_GO_bayesian_GO: A later implementation may preregister full deterministic Bayesian consensus reproduction.
decision_policy.experimental_covariance_GO_bayesian_NO_G: Proceed next with an n=4 experimental covariance/correlated-estimator certificate only; do not claim reproduction of the paper's final Bayesian consensus.
decision_policy.experimental_covariance_NO_GO: Stop before estimator implementation and report the missing source information.

GO_requirements: all four measurement identities and central values are explicitly source-located
all four relative standard uncertainties are explicitly source-located
all six pairwise correlations are explicitly source-located
the declared matrix is symmetric with unit diagonal and positive definite
conversion from relative uncertainty/correlation to the chosen covariance representation is specified without hidden fitted quantities
no terminal BIPM comparison or published NIST consensus value is required to construct the covariance object
A_experimental_covariance.question: Do the paper's four values, four standard uncertainties, and six off-diagonal correlation coefficients uniquely determine a valid four-dimensional experimental covariance object suitable for deterministic generalized correlated-estimator work?

GO_requirements: measurement-error likelihood and its full covariance are explicit
all prior families and parameterizations are explicit
posterior computation is uniquely specified or analytically reproducible
sample size/seed/burn-in/thinning/convergence choices are either irrelevant by analytic construction or explicitly specified
Huber M and Qn conventions are fully specified enough to give a unique deterministic artifact
B_published_bayesian_consensus.NO_GO_rule: Any materially result-driving computational or statistical choice absent from the primary source is recorded as an explicit reconstruction blocker rather than filled with a conventional assumption.
B_published_bayesian_consensus.question: Does the paper specify a unique deterministic procedure sufficient to reproduce equation (64) and its uncertainty without inventing unstated sampler, likelihood, prior-parameterization, convergence, or robust-summary details?

known_prior_information.allowed_claim: The audit may classify reconstruction layers as GO or NO-GO based only on source completeness and deterministic identifiability; it must not interpret a numerical discrepancy as evidence for new physics or apparatus failure.
known_prior_information.reason: Before this freeze, the project discussion exposed the paper's final reported G, its large discrepancy from BIPM-14, and the existence of a four-configuration Bayesian hierarchical consensus with dark uncertainty. This PR is a source/estimator feasibility audit, not a blind result discovery.

objective: Determine, without performing a BIPM-vs-NIST common-constant comparison, which layers of the NIST 2026 BIPM-torsion-balance redetermination are sufficiently specified for deterministic reconstruction: (A) the four-configuration experimental covariance object and (B) the published Bayesian hierarchical consensus.

primary_source.publication: Stephan Schlamminger et al., Redetermination of the gravitational constant with the BIPM torsion balance at NIST

scientific_constraints: Do not infer independence from absent covariance entries; Table 18 is the authoritative correlation surface.
Do not replace the published Bayesian consensus with a generalized least-squares average and call it a reproduction of equation (64).
Do not use the BIPM-14 central value, NIST equation (64), CODATA value, or any cross-publication discrepancy to decide experimental covariance feasibility.
Preserve the distinction between experimental covariance (Tables 16/18) and dark-uncertainty hierarchy (equation 63/Table 19).
Do not cross the HUST AAF E-001 evidence-classification boundary.

consensus_layer.configuration_effect_distribution: lambda ~ N(0, Sigma), with Sigma_ij = tau_i tau_j R_ij
consensus_layer.published_summary_method: Huber's M for consensus location and Qn for uncertainty, applied to large samples from the posterior distribution of mu

experimental_layer.paper_statement: Several input variables enter more than one measurement, so the four measured values of G are correlated; Table 18 lists the corresponding correlation coefficients.
